highlights.text: She knew that all men who were not part of her father’s band were called cocksuckers and all women who would not go with them were called pigfuckers, although she was not quite sure—and did not much care—what these insults really meant.
That was not the end of the problems, but it was the beginning of solutions.
People who did not have enough to do could easily become so lazy that they skimped what little work they did have,
excessive pride is a familiar sin, but a man may just as easily frustrate the will of God through excessive humility.”
“You fool, if you don’t take the money I’ll run you through with my sword and fuck her in front of the children!”
Tom was one of those people who kept his religion deep in his heart. Sometimes they were the best kind.
The world of power and property required that a man be suspicious, demanding, and insistent.
Having faith in God did not mean sitting back and doing nothing. It meant believing that you would find success if you did your best honestly and energetically.

William returned to practical matters. “There must be thirty quarrymen there, some with their wives and children,” he said. “So what?” “There may be bloodshed.” Waleran raised his black eyebrows. “Indeed?” he said. “Then I shall give you absolution.”
The first casualty of a civil war was justice, Philip had realized.
There were not many people who said what they meant and did what they said.
“I wonder if he could be made to see reason.” “What do you mean?” “God is supposed to be merciful—perhaps monks should be too.”
“Who was the priest?” he said urgently. “His name was Waleran Bigod. He’s now the bishop of Kingsbridge.” Jack gave a sigh of profound satisfaction. “And he’s still alive,” he said.
Waleran said: “The worst mistake I ever made was to help Philip become prior.”

Until this moment there had been an element of unreality about the whole thing; but now the men who wanted to burn Kingsbridge were right there, riding along the road, and suddenly the danger was hideously real.

They existed because earls and kings felt the need of them. Philip may be a damned fool on matters of love and marriage, Jack thought, but at least he’s found a way to rule a community without the help of savages like these. It was an odd moment for such reflections. Was this the kind of thing men thought about when they were about to die?
Waleran narrowed his eyes. “I can’t make out whether you love that wretched woman or hate her.” “No,” William said. “Nor can I.”

“You know me, and you know my brother; and you’ve chosen Alfred. You know Prior Philip, and you know Earl William; and you’ve chosen William. All I have left to say to you is that you deserve everything you’re going to get.”

“Perhaps the savages will always be in control,” Philip said gloomily. “Perhaps greed will always outweigh wisdom in the councils of the mighty; perhaps fear will always overcome compassion in the mind of a man with a sword in his hand.”
William hated nothing more than the feeling that people were laughing at him behind their hands. He had spent his life forcing people to respect him and his family,
He had to learn that those who treated him in a hostile way did so out of weakness. He saw the hostility and reacted angrily, instead of seeing the weakness and giving reassurance.
I lost in court, he thought, but that was only about stones. What I gained was something infinitely more valuable. Today I won a man’s soul.
“I’ve seen better men die,” he said. “I’ve killed men who deserved it less.”
Jack’s look said You and me, together, always; and Aliena thought At last. It felt very peaceful.

He was the worst kind of Christian, Philip realized: he embraced all of the negatives, enforced every proscription, insisted on all forms of denial, and demanded strict punishment for every offense; yet he ignored all the compassion of Christianity, denied its mercy, flagrantly disobeyed its ethic of love, and openly flouted the gentle laws of Jesus. That’s what the Pharisees were like, Philip thought; no wonder the Lord preferred to eat with publicans and sinners.
“Knotty theological questions are the least worrying of problems, to me.” “Why?” “Because they will all be resolved in the hereafter, and meanwhile they can safely be shelved.”
